socket.note: v0.9 fix round (2026-10-28, reviewer defects) (reviewer: 'coupler-to-horn fastening has no room'): the flange is a SOCKET for the stock horn - a slot through the flange (open at both ends along the horn arms, width = horn arm_w_ASSUMED + slot_fit, from the hub end face to over_arm_plane past the horn's arm plane, with a relief of horn collar_d + collar_relief_dia for the horn's round hub at the arm level and its spline collar). slot_fit 0.05 = print, then hand-fit the slot to the arms (each 0.1 mm of fit is ~1 deg of vane play peak to peak). Torque goes through the arm flanks (no screws); the arms can slide along the slot (they lie along v at neutral, the direction the foam pad pushes the servo), so the coupler takes no side load. The slot floor stays horn_axial_gap short of the arm face so the coupler never pushes the horn axially

set_screw.size: M2 x 3 set screw, cup point (0.9 mm hex key)
set_screw.note: v0.9 fix round (2026-10-28, reviewer defects) (reviewer: 'vane + integral shaft has no axial retention', 'D-flat lost motion'): one M2 set screw through the coupler hub (at mid shaft engagement, along -v from the +v side) onto the shaft's D-flat. It fixes the coupler on the shaft axially (the vane can move only until the hub meets the boss face, boss_gap, or the vane root meets the duct wall) and removes the D-flat rotational play. key_d x key_len = the hex-key access envelope checked in C5

C28 checks float >= tolerance, the axes, the coupler sweep, the axial retention and the foam (v0.9 fix round (2026-10-28, reviewer defects))

fairing.lintel_note: the service opening stops lintel_h under the pocket ceiling: a strip of the service-side wall (lintel) carries the ceiling, so the ceiling bridges the pocket width onto it and the lintel bridges the opening length when the module prints upright - no support (with supports on, the slicer also supported the closed cavities of the duct and liner: 73 g of support, measured). The servo with its connector half slides out under the lintel.
fairing.note: fin-root fairing (part of propulsion_module, Layout.fair_*): a box around the servo pocket in the fin frame (u radial at the fin theta, v tangential, Z), from the duct surface to the case bottom + servo_float + outer_block, Z from the lower ear tab's slot floor - floor_t to the pocket top + top_t; a 45 deg keel under it down to the fin plate (prints upright with no support under the fairing). The pocket is open on the service_side (+v = +theta) face and closed by the printed servo_cover; the servo (with the coupler and horn on it) slides in along -v with its lower ear tab in a floor slot that holds it radially and vertically. The pocket's ceiling is a cantilever when the module prints upright: tree supports inside the four pockets (removed through the open side). Above the case: the lead bay (connector_lwh_ASSUMED; was the inline-connector bay until 2026-11-18 - the lead is no longer cut: it leaves through the tunnel in the pocket's side wall into the joint pod, servo_leads.joint_pod). The fin plate passes through the fairing (the pocket cuts it) and continues above and outboard of it unchanged: the fins stay the landing legs (footprint unchanged).
fairing.connector_lwh_note: 2026-11-18 (servo-lead fix): there is no inline connector any more - this box over the case (same size, the fairing is unchanged) is the lead bay: the factory lead runs from the case end over the case to the tunnel in the pocket's side wall; the plug itself passes the pocket from the open service side straight into the tunnel

cover.note: printed servo_cover (class C, flat): a plate on the fairing's service face; two screws along -v into tap holes in the fairing's inner wall (beside the hinge boss, below the lead pipe) and outer block; C5 checks the tap material and a screwdriver path (driver_d x driver_len along +v)

Compared with servo.torque_kgcm_4v8 in C28.

bushing.model: brass tube 6 x 0.45 mm (K&S type), cut to the boss length + protrude_into_duct
bushing.protrude_note: vane fix 2026-11-17: the bushing stands 0.95 mm proud of the duct's inner wall (7.95 mm long instead of 7.0), into the 2.0 mm gap between the vane's outer edge and the duct wall, so the vane's OUTWARD stop is its edge on the bushing end ~1.05 mm out (C28 measures it) instead of the duct wall 2.0 mm out. 0.95, not more: C8 keeps the exhaust path D(duct_id - 2) = r 44.0 free of everything but the vanes / shafts (a 1.5 mm protrusion put 3.6 mm^3 of each bushing into it - C8 FAIL, measured). The coupler's socket sits in the ~4 mm between the stock horn's arms and the servo's output tower and cannot take 2 mm of axial travel plus clearance (docs/v0.9_CAD_변경.md, vane fix). The bushing replaces the bare shaft in that gap (O6 vs O5 across the 2 mm tip gap): no change to the vane or the duct. Assembly: press it in from the duct side until 0.95 mm stands proud (a 0.95 mm gauge, cad/exports/print/vane_fit_test)

vane_drive.fix_2026_11_17_note: vane fix 2026-11-17, user report (verbatim): '현재 너가 설계했던 vane 부분에서 서보모터가 너의 생각보다 커서 조립이 제대로 되지 않는 문제가 발생했어 ... 조립이 원활하지 않은 부분은 다시 계산해서 만들어줘' / '서보는 포켓에 들어가는데 혼, 커플러가 서보모터 와 프레임 사이에 들어가지 않아. 여유 공간이 없어.' What was wrong: the case was placed from servo.arm_plane_bottom_from_bottom 27.5 (never measured), which put the stock horn's face 29.3 mm above the case bottom; the vendor drawing gives 35.5 (servo.stock_horn_top_from_bottom) - the real horn sat 6.2 mm into the coupler (110 mm^3 overlap on the solids), its screw head 3.8 mm into the vane shaft, the servo's output tower into the coupler socket, and servo + horn + coupler was 3.4 mm longer than the pocket (no insertion path at all). The CAD also modelled no output tower / gear cover (only a O6 boss) and no axial clearance budget. Fix: the case is placed from the real horn height (+4.2 mm radially outward), hub 8 -> 6 (vane shaft 2 mm shorter), slot floor -> horn face 2.2, fairing top 1.6 -> 1.4, horn dims E from the drawing, the servo's top modelled (servo.top_envelope_E), the bushing protrudes 0.95 mm into the duct as the vane's outward stop, C28 measures the assembly clearance with the upper-tolerance horn (>= 1.0 mm) and the insertion path on the solids; set the coupler with the vane on its outward stop and a set_shim_t shim (Layout.dd_set_shim) between the pocket's inner wall and the hub
vane_drive.set_shim_note: vane fix 2026-11-17: assembly gauge - with the vane pulled out against the bushing end (outward stop), a Layout.dd_set_shim thick U-shim between the pocket's inner wall and the coupler hub puts the coupler at its design position when the set screw is tightened (printed with the fit test, cad/cadquery/make_vane_fit_test.py)

servo_leads.note: v0.6 vane-servo lead route (SPEC 3.8 / 5.1, edf.mount = tabs only): pod window -> outside up beside the fin -> vertical entry slot through the shoulder ring / cone skin into the sleeve-skin annulus, one straight column per lead -> deck notch -> spigot-ring rebate (under the intake skirt) round to gather_theta_deg -> intake servo channel + bulge past the EDF bell -> shelf notch -> along the strut -> bulkhead servo hole -> avionics bay. Ribbon and mass values are ASSUMED (26 AWG 3-core flat silicone servo wire): measure and weigh the wire you buy. | 2026-11-18 (servo-lead fix): factory MG90S lead + standard extension, nothing cut - see fix_2026_11_18_note.
servo_leads.fix_2026_11_18_note: servo-lead fix 2026-11-18, user report 2026-11-17 (verbatim): 'intake moduel의 서보모터 배선을 진행 할 떄, 커넥터가 지나가지 못해서 배선을 잘랐다가 이어야하는 문제가 있어. 이 문제는 propulsion_module이 모듈에서도 같은 문제가 발생했어. 해당 문제를 수정해줘. 커넥터를 자르지 않아도 케이블을 통과시켜 조립할 수 있도록 말이야.' Cause (measured on the solids of b42975c, connector-envelope sweep): the route was sized for the bare ribbon (ribbon_w/t_ASSUMED + min_clearance): the O4.8 pipe tunnel, the 4.6 x 2.4 entry slot, the annulus column between its 4.6 mm guide walls, the 4.6 x 3.0 deck notch, the 9 x 3.6 intake channel and the 6 mm gate all block the 8.15 x 4.0 factory plug (overlap 39-318 mm^3), and the design assumed the MG90S lead CUT to 40 mm with an inline connector in the fairing and a hand-made extension crimped after threading. The annulus column cannot simply grow: the clock keyways sit every ~13 deg round the sleeve and every widening of the column's guide walls (even to 6 mm) breaks the keyway plan / the lead-passage fence (Layout raises). Fix (no cutting, off-the-shelf parts only): (1) the factory plug passes ONE closed passage, a short O tunnel through the fairing's side wall into (2) a joint pod on the duct below the shoulder (open outward, inside the body's shadow r <= body_r) where the plug meets a standard servo extension (joint_pod; the unused factory lead is folded there); (3) every other propulsion passage is LAID IN from outside: a keyhole slit (keyhole.slit_w) through the cone / body skin over the entry slot and the column, the ribbon pressed in edge-on and turned flat behind it; at the top it leaves through the slit, passes over the deck seat (the deck stays whole: the deck notch's through-hole is gone) and under the intake skirt through skirt_notch into the old notch groove on the spigot and the rebate; (4) intake: a lip slit (lip_slit) opens the servo channel toward the inside like the motor-lead slit, the gate is laid in from below, and the extension's socket goes STRAIGHT UP through the open interior and a connector-size bulkhead hole to J8-J11 (C43 sweeps the connector envelope through every passage it passes and checks the lengths).
servo_leads.lead_exit_note: MG90S lead leaves the case end face opposite the output shaft, near the bottom (i.e. at +v in the pod frame, away from the vane horn / pushrod). Verify on the unit before printing: 'shaft_end' has no route (layout raises).

The MG90S lead ends in a 3-pin 2.54 mm JR-style female housing (F: vendor listings). ridge_A: a latch / key ridge or a molded strain relief on the servo's own plug (Futaba-J style) - not on the drawing (A). strain_relief_A: rigid length of the wire crimp / heat-shrink behind the housing (A). mated_len_E: the servo plug inserted into the 18 mm shroud (~6 mm of the housing outside it) + the strain relief (E)

fin.stability_note: 2026-11-18 stability fix (user: '시뮬레이션상 안정하도록 모델을 수정해줘' - make the vehicle stable in the simulations): span 76 -> 125, tip_chord 60 -> 45, root chord 90 and the TE on the exit plane kept, straight leading edge root LE z 90 -> tip LE z 45 (aero planform = the stability study's K1: OpenRocket = RocketPy static margin >= 1.0 cal with the CanSat, and without it with the nose ballast; runs/stability/study). ilink.note: FCU USART1 <-> COM USART0, 8N1, U2X = 0 (UBRR 3: 0 % error at 16 MHz). Frame 0xC5 0x5C LEN TYPE payload CRC16-CCITT-FALSE (SPEC 10.4). Both boards on the 5 V logic UBEC, common ground

nlink.note: NAV = SPI master (fosc/8 = 2 MHz, mode 0, MSB first) -> FCU = SPI slave (interrupt per byte); one fixed-length full-duplex exchange per NAV tick, pushed when the navigation state is ready; byte_gap_us between bytes gives the FCU's slave interrupt time to load its next return byte (SPEC 10.5, src/core/nlink_proto.h). (v0.6.3 co-simulation: the NAV frame time moves by up to 0.45 ms at the pad -> flight switch; a fallback tick that starts later than ~4.6 ms leaves the FCU background no time and drops flight records (A/B: 4.6 ms 0 dropped, 4.7 ms 1, 5.0 ms 2-4), so frame_timeout_ms = 4.6 keeps 0.15 ms of margin on both sides.) If no complete frame arrives within frame_timeout_ms of the previous tick the FCU runs the tick on its own Timer2 with the navigation data invalid (imu_ok = baro_ok = false -> I9 after the supervisor's failure time)
nlink.exchange_watchdog_note: v0.9 firmware round (fw09/spec W1): the NAV master's interrupt-paced exchange (72 Timer3 compare-B interrupts, ~632 us on the chip; measured SS low 618-621 us in single-chip simavr, 636-641 us in the 4-core co-sim with the interrupt response) is closed by the main loop when it has not ended exchange_watchdog_us after its start (Timer3 restarts at 0 each exchange): compare off, SS high, one trip counted; the FCU sees one missing frame (resync / timeout tick). Must exceed 1.5 x the exchange and stay below the tick minus the push floor (generator checks). Chosen value, not a measurement.

esp_bridge.uart_note: the same 8N1 baud on the COM's USART1 (U2X 0: UBRR 25, +0.16 %), on both ESPs' UART0 and on the ground PC's serial port; 38400 because it is within 0.2 % on the 16 MHz AVR with U2X 0 (57600 is not: +2.1 % with U2X 0, -0.8 % with U2X 1) and well inside the BSS138 channels' 10k pull-up rise time (carrier spec level_shifting.speed_note: fine up to 115200); a 47-byte TELEM v5 is 12.2 ms on the wire (E)
esp_bridge.boot_note: the COM holds the ESP's RST low (PC6) from its first instructions, for reset_hold_ms in radio_init, then releases it and drops every UART byte for boot_discard_ms (the ESP8266 ROM boot log at 74880 baud; the bridge sketch is up after ~100-300 ms, A); the ESP sends no ready byte - a request before the bridge is up is a lost packet for the ground. 2026-11-06 review: only on a cold COM boot (power-on, or no reset flag); after a COM watchdog / brown-out / external reset the ESP is left running and no window opens (as the Ebyte module, which a COM reset does not touch). PC6 is open-drain: driven low to hold RST, released to input (Hi-Z) - the Q5 pull-ups raise RST, so a manual RST-GND short never shorts a driven-high pin
esp_bridge.air_rate_note: 2026-11-10: the ESP-NOW bit rate the link model (sim/link_model.py esp_bridge) times the frames at - 1 Mbps 802.11b DSSS, long preamble (A, as bit_rate_note: measure on the real ESPs; a higher rate only shortens the ~1 ms on air, the round trip is dominated by the two 38400-baud UART hops per direction)
